diagnostics.message:
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
module.github_app_runner_group reads the tenant's CI/CD secrets (app key, app id, installation id) by name via data "aws_secretsmanager_secret"/"aws_secretsmanager_secret_version" inside the submodule, but nothing orders those reads after aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.cicd_secrets, which creates the seed (AWSCURRENT) versions in this same configuration. On a first apply the submodule's data sources will be read before the secrets/versions exist and fail.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
module.github_app_runner_group reads the CI/CD secrets (data.aws_secretsmanager_secret.secrets / data.aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.secrets) by name only; those secrets are created and seeded in this same module tree by aws_secretsmanager_secret.cicd_secrets / aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.cicd_secrets. Nothing orders the submodule's data reads after secret creation/seeding, so on a first apply the reads can race and fail. Add `depends_on = [aws_secretsmanager_secret.cicd_secrets, aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.cicd_secrets]` on the `module "github_app_runner_group"` block.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
`module.github_app_runner_group` reads its secrets via `data "aws_secretsmanager_secret" "secrets"` looked up by name (`${var.secrets_prefix}...`), where `var.secrets_prefix` is built only from `var.tenant`/`var.deployment_config`. No attribute reference or depends_on ties the module to the secrets created and seeded by this configuration (`aws_secretsmanager_secret.cicd_secrets` / `aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.cicd_secrets`), so on a fresh apply the data reads execute before the secrets and their seed versions exist and the plan fails. The root module's own `data_cicd_secrets` data sources carry exactly this depends_on, but this module does not.

module.github_global_lock reads the tenant's CI/CD secrets (app key, app id, installation id) by name via data "aws_secretsmanager_secret"/"aws_secretsmanager_secret_version" inside the submodule, but nothing orders those reads after aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.cicd_secrets, which creates the seed (AWSCURRENT) versions in this same configuration. On a first apply the submodule's data sources will be read before the secrets/versions exist and fail.

----------------------------------------

module.github_global_lock reads the CI/CD secrets (data.aws_secretsmanager_secret.secrets / data.aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.secrets) by name only; those secrets are created and seeded in this same module tree by aws_secretsmanager_secret.cicd_secrets / aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.cicd_secrets. Nothing orders the submodule's data reads after secret creation/seeding, so on a first apply the reads can race and fail. Add `depends_on` referencing those resources on the `module "github_global_lock"` block.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
`module.github_global_lock` reads its secrets via `data "aws_secretsmanager_secret" "secrets"` looked up by name (`${var.secrets_prefix}...`), with no dependency on the secrets created and seeded in this configuration (`aws_secretsmanager_secret.cicd_secrets` / `aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.cicd_secrets`). On a fresh apply the by-name data lookups run before the secrets exist, causing a plan failure; the clean-global-lock lambda's IAM policy also references these data versions.

module.github_actions_job_logs reads the CI/CD secrets (data.aws_secretsmanager_secret.secrets / data.aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.secrets) by name only; those secrets are created and seeded in this same module tree by aws_secretsmanager_secret.cicd_secrets / aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.cicd_secrets. Nothing orders the submodule's data reads after secret creation/seeding, so on a first apply the reads can race and fail. Add `depends_on` referencing those resources on the `module "github_actions_job_logs"` block.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
`module.github_actions_job_logs` reads its secrets via `data "aws_secretsmanager_secret" "secrets"` looked up by name (`${var.secrets_prefix}...`), with no dependency on the secrets created and seeded in this configuration (`aws_secretsmanager_secret.cicd_secrets` / `aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.cicd_secrets`). On a fresh apply the by-name data lookups run before the secrets exist, causing a plan failure; the lambdas' IAM policy documents also reference these data versions, so the whole module needs to be ordered after seeding.
